formNote.palafinhero: On = Hero Form, off = Zero Form (when it first comes in). In practice it fights as Hero Form after switching out once, so it is on by default. The battle screen switches automatically.
formNote.aegislashblade: On = stats and damage taken while in Blade Forme (after it attacked first in the same turn). Its own attacks always use Blade Forme either way.
formNote.morpekohangry: On = Hangry Mode: Aura Wheel becomes Dark-type (Electric in Full Belly Mode). Base stats are the same. The battle screen switches it every turn.
formNote.castform: Castform's form follows the weather (Sunny = sun, Rainy = rain, Snowy = snow). Clicking one switches the weather used for the calculation.
formNote.mimikyubusted: On = Disguise already broken. Off = the first hit is blocked and it takes only 1/8 of max HP.

est.title: Opponent estimate
est.transformed: Transformed — its stats are copied, so nothing to estimate.
est.infeasible: No spread fits the inputs — check item, ability, critical hit and damage
est.scarfRuledOut: A damage-boosting item is confirmed → no Choice Scarf
est.note: Narrows each time a turn is applied. Damage dealt is checked against the before/after HP % (the game rounds down), damage taken allows ±1 HP, and correcting end-of-turn HP to the game value narrows HP; multi-hit, fixed-damage moves and turns with a hit-triggered item are skipped. Uses the entered ability. Battle damage tables and the expected flow also use this range instead of the nature and SP on the team preview.

For confusion self-hits or other, enter the HP lost (yours in HP, the opponent in %)

battle.pctRangeHint: The game shows opponent HP % rounded down, so the actual damage is somewhere in this range. Stat estimation checks the damage possible from the before/after %
battle.hpCheckHint: If the end-of-turn HP (sandstorm, Leftovers, etc.) differs from the game, enter the game value. It is used to estimate the opponent HP stat
battle.spHint: Stat points (for the opponent, the range matching the estimated stat — includes every nature effect when unknown)

rec.doublesHint: Doubles: an approximation that pairs each of your active Pokémon 1:1 with each opposing active Pokémon for this turn and adds them up. Opposing single-target moves are assumed to aim more at whichever of your two Pokémon suits them better. Both-slot combos recheck combined damage when both hit the same target. Ally support effects aren't considered.
rec.scoreHelp: Scores are in HP %. HP the opponent lost − HP you lost, plus KOs (weight "KO"), hazards, and the post-turn matchup outlook (1 turn) or the best next-turn value (2–3 turns), averaged over the expected opponent choices. Positive favours you; compare values between options.
rec.applyBothHint: Put into both slots' actions this turn

help.title: How to use
help.flow1: On the Party screen, set ability, nature, item, Stat Points and moves for your 6 Pokémon. Everything is saved in your browser.
help.flow2: On Singles or Doubles Team Preview, enter the opponent's 6 Pokémon and tap yours to set the bring order.
help.flow3: On the Battle screen, enter each turn's actions and results; HP, stat stages and field effects are tracked for you.
help.calc1: Level 50, IVs 31. HP = base + SP + 75; other stats = (base + SP + 20) × nature.
help.calc2: Damage follows the Gen 9 formula (power, stats, STAB, type matchup, weather, terrain, crits, items, abilities) with 16 random rolls (85–100%) for KO chances.
help.calc3: Spread moves that hit multiple targets in doubles deal 0.75×.
help.data1: Pokémon, move and item data: Pokémon Showdown (Champions mod); localized names: PokeAPI
help.data2: Images: Pokémon Champions in-game sprites (Bulbagarden Archives)
help.limits1: Some special ability or item effects may not be reflected in calculations.
help.limits2: Moves marked * next to PP use an estimated Champions PP value.
help.flow4: In battle, enter who moved first and the damage dealt and taken; the opponent's speed (Scarf / nature) and bulk and attack spreads narrow down every turn.
help.flow5: The Stats Table lets you search and compare bulk, the best attack of each type, and speed tiers (with Scarf, Tailwind, Sticky Web and abilities) for every allowed Pokémon.

perf.title: Pokémon Stats Table
perf.sub: {n} Pokémon allowed in {reg} (Mega Evolutions included) · Level 50

power.note: Attack index = power × Atk (SpA) stat × STAB × ability (no item, Mega Evolutions hold their Mega Stone, no weather or terrain). A/C = Attack SP for physical moves, Special Attack SP for special moves (Body Press uses Defense). Moves with a drawback unchecked above are never picked; if the picked move has a drawback, the best drawback-free move that never misses is shown below it. Abilities are chosen to maximise the index and shown only when they matter (Skill Link = always 5 hits). Multi-hit moves with a random hit count show the expected value by hit-count probability (top) and min–max (bottom), assuming the move hits: 2–5 hits are 35/35/15/15%, Population Bomb and Triple Axel check accuracy again from the second hit. Moves that use the target's stats (Foul Play) or whose power depends on the target (weight, HP, …) are excluded.

bulk.note: Bulk index = HP stat × Def (SpD) stat ÷ 0.411 (same formula as the Party screen). H = HP, B = Def, D = SpD SP; nature = a Def (SpD) boosting nature. The stage applies to Def and SpD. No ability or item modifiers.

speed.legend: S = Speed SP, nature = Speed-boosting nature, Scarf = Choice Scarf ×1.5 (— for Mega Evolutions, which hold their Mega Stone). Ability rows assume the condition is met (Swift Swim, Chlorophyll, Sand Rush, Slush Rush, Surge Surfer, Unburden ×2; Quick Feet ×1.5; Speed Boost +1 stage). Unburden is not combined with Scarf.

perf.rangeHint: For multi-hit moves with a random hit count: top = expected value by hit-count probability, bottom = min–max
perf.loadedDiceHint: Calculated as if holding Loaded Dice: 2–5 hit moves hit 4 or 5 times (50% each), Population Bomb 4–10 times, Triple Axel all 3 hits. Not applied to Mega Evolutions (they hold a Mega Stone). Acrobatics loses its no-item doubling.

stats.title: Stat basics
items: Level is fixed at 50 and all IVs are 31.
Instead of EVs you distribute Stat Points: up to 32 per stat, 66 in total.
A nature raises one non-HP stat by 10% and lowers another by 10% (some natures change nothing).

stab.title: STAB (same-type attack bonus)
items: Moves that match one of the user’s types get 1.5× power.
With Adaptability it is 2× instead of 1.5×.
Protean and Libero change the user’s type to the move’s type right before it attacks, so it always gets STAB (once per switch-in).
If Mega Evolution changes the type, STAB uses the new type.
Status moves and fixed-damage moves are unaffected by STAB.

types.title: Type effectiveness
items: Super effective = 2×, not very effective = 0.5×, no effect = 0×.
With two types the multipliers stack: 4× and 0.25× are possible, and any immunity makes it 0×.
Immunities can change: Scrappy and Mind’s Eye let Normal and Fighting hit Ghost, Levitate and Air Balloon avoid Ground moves, and Roost removes the Flying type for that turn.
Some status moves fail because of type: Thunder Wave does not affect Ground types, and poisoning moves do not affect Poison or Steel types.

typeNotes.title: Type traits
items: Effects each type has besides effectiveness.

status.title: Status conditions
items: Burn: loses 1/16 of max HP at the end of each turn, physical damage halved (except Guts and Facade). Fire types cannot be burned.
Paralysis: Speed halved, 12.5% chance to be unable to move when using a move (lower than 25% in the main series). Electric types cannot be paralyzed.
Poison: 1/8 per turn. Bad poison: starts at 1/16 and grows by 1/16 each turn (up to 15/16), resetting to 1/16 on switch-out. Poison and Steel types cannot be poisoned.
Sleep: the first attempt to act always fails, the second wakes up 33% of the time, the third always wakes up. Sleep from Rest lasts through the second attempt.
Freeze: 25% chance to thaw on the first and second attempts, always thaws on the third. Being hit by a Fire-type attack or moves like Scald also thaws. Ice types cannot be frozen.
Only one status condition at a time, and it stays after switching. Volatile conditions such as confusion (33% self-hit) and infatuation (50% immobile) end when switching out.

weather.title: Weather
items: Lasts 5 turns, or 8 if set by a Pokémon holding the matching weather rock. New weather replaces the old one.
Sun: Fire moves 1.5×, Water moves 0.5×, no freezing, Solar Beam fires without charging.
Rain: Water moves 1.5×, Fire moves 0.5×, Thunder and Hurricane never miss.
Sandstorm: non-Rock/Ground/Steel Pokémon lose 1/16 of max HP each turn, Rock types get 1.5× Sp. Def.
Snow: Ice types get 1.5× Defense, Blizzard never misses (no end-of-turn damage).

terrain.title: Terrain
items: Only affects grounded Pokémon. Lasts 5 turns, or 8 if set by a Pokémon holding Terrain Extender.
Electric Terrain: Electric moves 1.3×, cannot fall asleep (Yawn included).
Grassy Terrain: Grass moves 1.3×, restores 1/16 of max HP each turn, Earthquake and Bulldoze deal 0.5×.
Misty Terrain: Dragon moves deal 0.5×, no status conditions or confusion.
Psychic Terrain: Psychic moves 1.3×, priority moves (+1 or higher) aimed at grounded Pokémon fail.

grounded.title: Ungrounded Pokémon
items: Flying types, Levitate, Air Balloon holders and Pokémon under Magnet Rise are not grounded.
Ground moves miss them, and they ignore terrain effects, Spikes, Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web.
Gravity, being hit by Smack Down, or Ingrain makes them grounded.

crit.title: Critical hits
items: 1.5× damage.
Ignores the attacker’s stat drops and the target’s stat boosts, and ignores Reflect, Light Screen and Aurora Veil. Burn still halves damage.
Chance: stage 0 = 1/24, +1 = 1/8, +2 = 1/2, +3 or more = always. High-crit moves +1, Super Luck and Scope Lens +1, Focus Energy +2.
Battle Armor and Shell Armor block critical hits.

ranks.title: Stat stages
items: Accuracy and evasion: (3 + stage) / 3, using your accuracy stage minus the target’s evasion stage.
All stat stages reset when switching out.

order.title: Turn order
items: Switching happens before moves. Higher-priority moves go first; within the same priority the faster Pokémon moves first, and ties are random.
Under Trick Room (5 turns) slower Pokémon move first within the same priority. Priority itself is unchanged.
Speed modifiers: stat stages, Choice Scarf 1.5×, Tailwind 2× (4 turns), paralysis 1/2.
Mega Evolution happens at the start of the turn, so the Mega’s Speed already decides order on the turn it evolves.

damage.title: Damage
items: Damage is randomly one of 16 rolls between 85% and 100%. If all 16 rolls KO it is a guaranteed KO; if only some do, it is a possible (random) KO.
Reflect (physical), Light Screen (special) and Aurora Veil (both) halve damage, or about 2/3 in Doubles.
Since everyone is level 50, the same move’s damage depends on the attacker’s Attack (Sp. Atk) and the target’s HP and Defense (Sp. Def).

doubles.title: Double battles
items: Spread moves (all foes / all others) deal 0.75× when they hit two or more Pokémon.
Moves that hit "all others", like Earthquake, also hit your ally.
Helping Hand: ally’s move 1.5× power. Friend Guard: ally takes 0.75× damage.
If the chosen target faints first, a single-target move goes to the remaining foe.

mega.title: Mega Evolution
items: Once per battle, only for one Pokémon holding its Mega Stone.
Mega Evolution changes base stats and Ability, and for some Pokémon the type. Base HP stays the same.
Mega Stones cannot be removed or swapped (Trick and similar moves fail).

grass: Immune to powder and spore moves (Sleep Powder, Poison Powder, Stun Spore, etc.) and not redirected by Rage Powder.
ice: Immune to Sheer Cold (which is also less accurate when used by non-Ice types).
poison: Cannot be poisoned or badly poisoned.
Toxic never misses when used by a Poison type.
A grounded Poison type removes Toxic Spikes from its side when it switches in.
flying: Not grounded, so unaffected by Spikes, Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web.
Loses the Flying type on the turn it uses Roost.
ghost: Can switch out despite trapping effects (Shadow Tag, binding moves, Jaw Lock, etc.), except its own Ingrain.
Curse costs 1/2 of its HP and makes the target lose 1/4 each turn (other types: Speed −1, Attack and Defense +1).
dark: Immune to status moves boosted by an opponent’s Prankster.
steel: Cannot be poisoned or badly poisoned.

electric: Electric Terrain: Electric moves used by grounded Pokémon 1.3×.
grass: Grassy Terrain: Grass moves used by grounded Pokémon 1.3×.
ground: Grassy Terrain: Earthquake and Bulldoze deal 0.5×.
flying: Not grounded, so unaffected by terrain.
Gravity: counts as grounded, so Ground moves hit and terrain, Spikes, etc. apply.
psychic: Psychic Terrain: Psychic moves used by grounded Pokémon 1.3×.
rock: Takes no sandstorm damage and gets 1.5× Sp. Def in sandstorm.
dragon: Misty Terrain: grounded Pokémon take 0.5× from Dragon moves.

usageStats.title: Usage Stats
usageStats.sub: Smogon monthly stats (Pokémon Showdown Champions formats, weighted for 1500+ rating) organized by season (regulation) and month. Not the in-game Ranked Battle stats
usageStats.changeHint: Rank change from the previous period (season: previous season; month: previous month, or the previous season for the first month)
usageStats.usageHint: Team usage: share of teams that include this Pokémon (rating-weighted)
